parseCheck.fromYourFile: These checks ran on the text we extracted from your file. An ATS uses its own reader, which may see some parts differently.

detail.sectionsAll: All {{n}} standard section headings were found ({{found}}).
detail.sectionsNone: No standard section headings were found. Most ATS split a résumé by headings such as Experience or Education; without them, your content may land in one block.
detail.contactHeaderOnly: Your email and phone sit only in the page header, which some ATS skip. Put them in the body of the first page too.
detail.contactBoth: Your email and phone number were both found in the text.
detail.contactBothLinkedIn: Your email, phone number and LinkedIn address were all found in the text.
detail.contactNone: No email or phone number was found in the text. If your file has them, they may sit in an image, a text box or a header that text extraction skips.
detail.contactEmailOnly: Your email was found, but no phone number in a standard format.
detail.contactPhoneOnly: Your phone number was found, but no email address in a standard format.
detail.datesMany: {{n}} different dates were found, so an ATS can likely work out your timeline and your time in each role.
detail.datesNone: No dates in a recognizable form (such as Jan 2020 or 2020-2023) were found. An ATS uses dates to work out your experience and any gaps.
detail.datesOne: Only one date was found. If you list several roles, most of them may be missing start and end dates an ATS can read.
detail.encodingOk: No broken characters were found in the extracted text.
detail.encodingBroken: Characters that failed to decode: {{n}}. A font in your PDF is probably not mapped to standard Unicode, and an ATS reading it the same way would see the same garbled text.
detail.iconsNone: No icon-font characters were found in the extracted text.
detail.iconsFound: Icon-font characters found: {{n}}. Templates often draw the phone, email and LinkedIn symbols with an icon font; an ATS sees a stray character there, not the icon.
detail.linesNormal: The text came out with normal line breaks (about {{chars}} characters a line).
detail.linesLong: The text came out with unusually long lines (about {{chars}} characters a line). A table or text box may have merged several lines; check that your bullets are not running together.
detail.linesFlat: The text came out with almost no line breaks (about {{chars}} characters a line), the sign of a table layout or text boxes flattened into one block. An ATS may lose your sections and bullets.
detail.layoutSingle: No multi-column layout was found: the text reads in one order.
detail.layoutColumns: A multi-column layout was found in your PDF. Text extractors read in file order, not visual order, so columns are often mixed together or read out of sequence.
